comparison: Perfect agreement on C1ql2 as a direct target of Bcl11b (C4, C32-C34). Both evaluations find the evidence from in situ hybridization, immunohistochemistry, and prior binding data fully supportive. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on the overexpression control (C45). OpenEval finds it supported by Western blot and EM data. Peer reviewers explicitly requested this control and accepted the results showing no artifacts from elevated C1ql2 in wildtype background.

Perfect agreement on negative results for synapse numbers and bouton complexity (C55-C57). Both evaluations accept these findings as valid evidence that C1ql2 rescue has limited scope and supports multiple downstream pathways from Bcl11b.

Agreement on forskolin experiment (C67-C69) implicating cAMP pathway. OpenEval notes some interpretive uncertainty about definitiveness, but peer reviewers accept the finding without challenge as evidence for downstream signaling mechanisms.

Agreement on K262E mutation disrupting Nrxn3 binding in vitro (C87-C91). Both evaluations accept the structural modeling and co-culture data. However, OpenEval suggests additional controls for binding specificity, while peer reviewers raise this as a more significant concern regarding postsynaptic ligands.

Agreement on C1ql3 specificity controls (C42-C44, C49). Both evaluations accept that C1ql3 overexpression does not rescue, demonstrating specificity of C1ql2 function. No concerns raised by either evaluation about these negative controls.

Partial agreement on C1ql2 rescue of vesicle recruitment and structural phenotypes (C27-C28, C35-C41, C46-C48, C50-C51, C62). OpenEval finds evidence well-supported. Peer reviewers affirm rescue findings but Reviewer 3 raises concern about absence of overexpression controls in wildtype (addressed by C45 data in R14/R3 pairing).

Divergent focus on vesicle phenotype details (C38, C46-C47, C50-C51). OpenEval finds EM data supportive of specific docking/recruitment deficits. Peer Reviewer 2 raises significant concerns that terminals appear aberrant with loss of reserve pool vesicles, suggesting phenotype may be more extensive than claimed.

Overlapping claims on LTP rescue (C28, C62) and basal transmission (C59-C60). OpenEval finds complete rescue of LTP with unaffected basal transmission strengthens specificity. Peer reviewers accept LTP rescue but Reviewer 2 questions how unchanged I-O curves are consistent with reduced synapse numbers (see R3/R12 pairing).

Disagreement on basal transmission interpretation (C59-C60, C79). OpenEval finds unchanged input-output curves support specificity of LTP phenotype. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly questions how unchanged I-O curves are possible given reduced synapse numbers, identifying an apparent contradiction requiring explanation.

Divergent evaluations of C1ql2 knockdown phenocopy (C29, C70-C80). OpenEval finds evidence well-supported across multiple methods. Peer Reviewer 3 raises significant concern about potential off-target effects from 4 distinct shRNAs, requesting rescue with RNAi-insensitive C1ql2 cDNA that was not provided, creating uncertainty.

Divergent evaluations of heterologous co-culture assays (C7, C30, C82-C86). OpenEval finds experimental design with Nrxn cTKO and selective rescue provides strong evidence for specificity. Peer Reviewer 3 questions whether assay tests the proposed model, noting C1ql2 acts as artificial postsynaptic ligand rather than testing presynaptic co-localization, creating substantial interpretive uncertainty.

Overlapping uncertainty about K262E in vivo function (C92-C97, C96-C103). OpenEval notes mutant fails to rescue vesicle recruitment but finds unexpected LTP rescue creates interpretive challenges. Peer reviewers question mutation specificity for Nrxn3 vs. other postsynaptic ligands, with incomplete testing of binding partners creating uncertainty about mechanism.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about K262E LTP rescue and pathway divergence (C98, C100-C103). OpenEval notes elevated fEPSP slopes suggest possible gain-of-function requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers question binding specificity and whether GluK2 retention fully explains LTP rescue, with both identifying incomplete resolution of unexpected findings.

Divergent evaluations of Nrxn3 deletion and C1ql2 localization (C104-C110, C94-C95, C105, C31). OpenEval finds data support pathway with Nrxn3 required for C1ql2 stabilization. Peer Reviewer 3 raises concerns that reduced C1ql2 protein levels confound interpretation and triple knockout lacks Nrxn3 specificity, creating uncertainty about whether phenotype is specifically due to loss of C1ql2-Nrxn3(25b+) interaction.

Overlapping uncertainty about Nrxn triple knockout interpretation (C109-C110). OpenEval finds data supportive but notes reduced C1ql2 localization without mRNA changes. Peer reviewers raise concerns about lack of Nrxn3 specificity in triple knockout and confounding effects of reduced C1ql2 levels on all measurements.

Both address C1ql2-Nrxn3 interaction requirement for localization (C31, C94-C95, C105). OpenEval finds evidence from two independent manipulations (K262E and Nrxn3 deletion) strengthens conclusion. Peer reviewers question whether reduced C1ql2 levels in Nrxn knockout confound localization measurements, creating interpretive uncertainty.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background/context claims (C1-C3, C10-C26, C64-C66, C81, C99, C112-C140) as supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focus on novel experimental findings rather than background claims.

OpenEval evaluates integrative summary conclusions (C52, C80, C111) as well-supported by convergent experimental evidence, noting C1ql2.K262E results suggest additional complexity. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these high-level summary statements found.
